negative_findings.description: No evidence found that PrJSC Ukrainian Processing Centre (EDRPOU 24747867) publishes procurement notices or acts as a Prozorro buyer.
negative_findings.result_summary: Ukrainian-language search combining the company name with 'Prozorro' and 'закупівлі' returned only registry-aggregator profiles (YouControl, Opendatabot, ua-region) and unrelated tenders. UPC is a private joint-stock company and is outside the Public Procurement Law's buyer scope.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A major processing-infrastructure operator in this cell is structurally invisible to tender-based collection; its technology purchases must be inferred from vendor announcements, NBU registers and financial statements instead.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated public tender/procurement section was located for the PROSTIR / NPSMU card scheme as a distinct buyer.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches in Ukrainian for ПРОСТІР/НПСМУ + тендер/закупівля returned scheme description pages on bank.gov.ua and prostir.gov.ua plus Wikipedia, but no scheme-level procurement notices. PROSTIR appears to procure through the NBU legal entity rather than separately.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Card-scheme technology purchases must be tracked under the NBU's own EDRPOU (00032106) rather than under a PROSTIR-branded buyer; a collection rule keyed on 'ПРОСТІР' as a buyer name would return nothing.

negative_findings.description: bank.gov.ua rejected an unauthenticated plain fetch with HTTP 403.
negative_findings.result_summary: GET https://bank.gov.ua/ua/about/procurements returned 403 Forbidden with no body. The site is widely linked and clearly operational, so this reads as WAF/bot defence rather than a dead endpoint — recorded as unverified, not dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single most authoritative source in this cell needs a browser-grade fetch path; a naive crawler would silently record the central bank's procurement hub as unavailable.

negative_findings.description: No explicit list of SEP participants as procurement buyers was retrieved in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: The NBU payment-systems register pages were identified as the likely home of SEP/PROSTIR participant lists, but the pages were not fetched because of the 403 on the parent domain. Participant enumeration remains outstanding.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The state-owned SEP participants (Oschadbank, Ukreximbank, Ukrgasbank, PrivatBank) are themselves Prozorro-obliged buyers of payment technology, and without the participant list their EDRPOU codes are not yet in the watchlist.

coverage_gaps.description: The buyer watchlist currently holds confirmed EDRPOU codes only for NBU (00032106) and the Banknote Printing and Minting Works (21575489). Other NBU-controlled entities (e.g. the cash-handling/collection and IT service subsidiaries) have not been enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch the NBU structure pages via a browser-grade client and cross-check against the EDR register to build the full family of NBU-controlled legal entities and their EDRPOU codes, then bulk-register them as Prozorro API filters.

coverage_gaps.description: No CPV code set has been established for the technology in scope (cash processing, sorting, minting, HSMs, card personalisation, payment-system software, certification services).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Derive the CPV list from a sample of known NBU/BMD tenders, then use CPV as the primary cross-buyer filter so relevant purchases by unforeseen buyers are still caught.

coverage_gaps.description: Central-bank purchases conducted outside Prozorro under statutory exemptions or wartime rules are not covered by any identified machine-readable source.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Monitor NBU's own procurement page, its annual report and TI-Ukraine reporting for exemption decisions; treat vendor press releases and trade press as compensating sources for non-published purchases.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of this cell is thin — English searching surfaced only Prozorro/OCP/TI meta-material, no NBU tender content.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat Ukrainian as the mandatory working language for tender-level collection and use English only for the NBU's own /en mirror and international donor-financed procurement (e.g. Ukraine Facility / IFI-funded purchases, which follow separate rules).

coverage_gaps.description: Purchases financed by IFIs/EU (Ukraine Facility) may follow donor procurement rules and appear on donor portals rather than, or in addition to, Prozorro.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout EBRD, World Bank, EIB and EU Ukraine Facility procurement notice portals for NBU/payment-infrastructure beneficiaries as a follow-up cell.

brief: For this cell the source landscape is unusually good: Ukraine's Prozorro system, its OpenProcurement API and the BI Prozorro analytics module give machine-readable, legally open coverage of the NBU (EDRPOU 00032106) and the Banknote Printing and Minting Works (EDRPOU 21575489) as buyers, with annual procurement plans providing the earliest signal and Spending/Є-data closing the loop on actual payments. Around that core sit strong secondary layers — DOZORRO and TI-Ukraine for contested or exempted purchases, Clarity/YouControl/Opendatabot for entity resolution and supplier snowballing, and authorised marketplaces as redundancy mirrors. The main structural blind spots are the private processing operators (notably PrJSC Ukrainian Processing Centre), which fall outside the Public Procurement Law entirely, the PROSTIR scheme, which has no separate buyer identity and must be tracked under the NBU itself, and any central-bank purchases made under statutory or wartime exemptions. bank.gov.ua — the most authoritative source here — returned 403 to a plain fetch and should be treated as bot-defended-but-live, requiring a browser-grade collection path rather than being marked dead.
_note_ukrainian_language_search: All primary discovery queries were run in Ukrainian; English was used only for the Prozorro API/analytics meta-layer.
